newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt prefers tax credit option for super fund.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt prefers tax credit option for super fund.

text.p: The New Zealand government on Thursday released a report by a working group set up to examine taxation of life insurance and superannuation fund savings, and said it prefered the option of using a tax credit.
At present, income earned by savings invested in such schemes is taxed at a flat and final 33 percent. This is paid by the life offices and superannuation funds on behalf of contributors.
"That disadvantages low and middle income savers who normally pay less than 33 percent," Treasurer Winston Peters and Finance Minister Bill Birch said in a joint statement.
In July 1996, the government set up a working group to investigate means of taxing the earnings of such schemes at a rate appropriate to each individual saver contributing to the scheme.

Peters and Birch said the working group reported in April. They said the government had considered the report, reached its view on the options and now wished to consult further with the public about its decision on a preferred approach.
"It is undesirable to tax the income from anybody's savings at more than the rate normally applied to their income," they said.
